title: Oller exits after allowing fourth-inning comeback, Lee Yi-ri replaces him in KBO playoff game
text:
Oller exits after allowing fourth-inning comeback, Lee Yi-ri replaces him in KBO playoff game - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 27일(화) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Oller exits after allowing fourth-inning comeback, Lee Yi-ri replaces him in KBO playoff game 
 입력 2026.10.27. 20:30 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 KIA Tigers pitcher Adam Oller couldn't withstand the Samsung Lions hitters' onslaught and was removed in the fifth inning.
 Oller started on the 27th in game 2 against the Samsung Lions in the 2026 Shinhan SOL KBO playoffs at Daegu Samsung Lions Park and recorded 4⅔ innings, five hits (one home run), one walk, four strikeouts and five runs allowed.
 In the bottom of the first, after retiring leadoff batter Kim Ji-chan with a flyout to left, Oller got Park Seung-gyu to ground out to third and struck out Koo Ja-wook to start the game with a three-up, three-down inning. In the second, with one out, he gave up a hit to Choi Hyoung-woo but induced a grounder to shortstop from Kim Young-woong to get the lead runner, and struck out Kang Min-ho to end the inning.
 With KIA leading 1-0 in the third, Oller issued a walk to leadoff batter Ryu Ji-hyuk and then faced a 1-out, runner-on-second threat after Lee Jay-hyun's sacrifice bunt. Kim Ji-chan was caught on a flyout to shortstop, but Park Seung-gyu delivered an RBI double to tie the game 1-1. He followed with an RBI base hit by Koo Ja-wook to take the lead, and then gave up a two-run home run to Choi Hyoung-woo.
 After another three-up, three-down inning in the fourth, Oller retired leadoff batters Lee Jay-hyun and Kim Ji-chan with flyouts in the fifth. However, he yielded an infield hit to Park Seung-gyu and was replaced by left-handed reliever Lee Eui-ri, ending his outing. Lee Eui-ri issued walks and hit batters, then allowed Choi Hyoung-woo an RBI walk, increasing Oller's runs allowed to five.
 Oller threw 96 pitches, mixing a fastball (51), sweeper (23), changeup (12), cutter (6) and curve (4). His fastball topped out at 153 km/h. Although batters gave up the first run, he yielded the lead and couldn't make it through the fifth inning, which was regrettable.
